plan.notes: Transcribed from the official CRC 'Broadcast Journalism A.A. Degree - Local GE' program map, Catalog Year 2026-2027, published August 25, 2026 (mapmaker.losrios.edu/Maps/7837/PublishedPdf). GE Pattern: CRC Local. Map states Total Units 59-62; lower bound 59 encoded = 15+15+15+14 (semester sums verified at lower bound: Sem 1 Area L2 3-4 -> 3; Sem 4 Area L7B 2-3 -> 2 and second elective 2-3 -> 2). LINKED 'NOT TAKEN' PAIRS: Semester 1 offers three or-choices (JOUR 310/JOUR 300; RTVF 330/RTVF 331; RTVF 312/RTVF 362). Semester 2 repeats the JOUR 310/JOUR 300 and RTVF 330/RTVF 331 pairs with the map footnote 'Enroll in course not taken in Semester 1' (modeled as or-choices with explanatory notes). The Semester 2 RTVF 312/RTVF 362 pair carries NO such footnote in the map, so it is modeled as a free or-choice (documented here). JOUR 310 is also listed as RTVF 300 (cross-listed). List A (minimum 6 units; two 3-unit slots sequenced in Semester 3): JOUR 351, JOUR 410 (eligibility for ENGWR 300; advisory co/pre-req JOUR 300, 335, 404 or PHOTO 302), PHOTO 301, RTVF 315, RTVF 319, RTVF 360, RTVF 376 (also listed as MKT 314), RTVF 498 Work Experience in Radio, Television and Film (0.5-4 units), COMM 480 Honors Seminar: Political Campaign Communication (also listed as HONOR 340; prerequisite ENGWR 300). Semester 4 3-unit elective footnote: 'If JOUR 310 is not completed' (take JOUR 310 there); otherwise an open elective. Semester 4 (2-3 unit) elective suggestion: RTVF 498 Work Experience in RTVD (2-3 units); lower bound 2 encoded. RTVF 380 advisory per map: JOUR 300, 'RTCF 362' (apparent typo for RTVF 362), RTVF 370, and ability to type — advisories documented here, never encoded as prerequisites. JOUR 300 advisory: eligible for ENGWR 300. Suggested electives (map sidebar): POLS 302, POLS 310, COMM 311, COMM 315, ECON 302. Elective units are determined by the number needed to total 60 units for graduation; refer to Course Number for the appropriate course level. Local Areas 1A and 2: map recommends meeting with a counselor. Students interested in transfer to a four-year university should meet with a CRC counselor to select and plan major courses.
